name: iqr
title: Estimates the interquartile range of a vector

origin.description: Estimates of the interquartile range for each row (column) in a matrix.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A numeric, integer, or logical vector or matrix. A matrix is treated as its column-major vector.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of elements to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If TRUE, missing values are excluded.
Additional arguments passed to stats::quantile, including type and fuzz.

origin.details: The value is stats::quantile at 0.75 minus the quantile at 0.25. Unlike stats::IQR, a missing value with na.rm FALSE returns NA_real_. An empty vector is NA_real_. A single value is 0.

translation.description: Estimates the interquartile range of a vector.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A logical, integer, or numeric vector, or a matrix. A matrix is read in column-major order. A double missing value is nan. An integer missing value is -2147483648.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: 1-based positions to include. None uses every element. Zero is dropped and a negative value excludes.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If true, missing values are dropped. If false, any missing value returns nan.

arguments.name: type
arguments.text: Quantile type 1 through 9 passed to stats::quantile. The default is 7.

arguments.name: fuzz
arguments.text: Fuzz passed to stats::quantile. None uses R's default.

translation.details: Subsets with the same 1-based rules as R's vector [, then calls the R 4.5 quantile at 0.25 and 0.75. An empty result is nan. One remaining value is 0.0.
translation.value: A Python float. A missing result is nan.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.iqr import iqr

iqr(np.arange(1, 11))
